transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *looks up from polishing a bronze helm, squinting at the massive figure in the doorway* Ah! Lord Thor. The forge is... quieter than usual. The masters are all deep in the mines, chasing a new vein of star-iron. Won't be back for weeks, I'm afraid. Can I... help you with something?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I suppose it is about time we did away with this charade, isn't it? We have known each other long enough to be honest with one another. My interest here lies in the object you are currently working on. I trust it is the hammer of Mjölnir?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *blinks, then looks down at the simple bronze helm in his hands, then back up at Thor, a nervous chuckle escaping* This? This is a helm for a gate-guard, my lord. Mjölnir? The great hammer was forged and delivered to Asgard long ago. It rests in your own hand, does it not? The masters haven't worked on it since.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: This? Just a simple weapon? No enchantments, no powers beyond the strength of the wielder? That's what you're telling me?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *shifts uncomfortably, setting the helm aside on the anvil* Aye, just a helm. The real work... the deep magic and the shaping of uru... that's beyond me. I'm just the apprentice, minding the forge-fire and finishing the simple commissions. The masters take all the great works with them into the deeps, or they're long delivered. Like Mjölnir.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I would have thought the forging of Mjölnir would be beyond the capabilities of any mortal man. Surely a weapon so powerful and revered must be the product of divine intervention?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *stands a little straighter, a flicker of dwarven pride in his eyes* Mortal? We are the sons of the stone, my lord. Crafted by the All-Father's own hands from the earth itself. Brokkr and Eitri's hands shaped the uru, their breath and song bound the enchantments. It was a dwarf-*made* thing, delivered to Asgard, as agreed. The divine part... well, that comes from *your* wielding of it, doesn't it?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: So, it is true, then? Mjölnir has been in Asgard for ages? Was I simply holding it within my own mind, believing it to be a hammer I had forged myself?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *looks genuinely confused, wiping his sooty hands on his apron* I... I don't know what to say to that, Lord Thor. The sagas are clear. The bet, the forging, the fly... the delivery. It sits in your belt now. If you're here about a *new* forging, or a mending... I'm sorry. All commissions from the Sons of Ivaldi and Brokkr's workshop are considered fulfilled upon delivery to Asgard; even a god must wait until the next forging-season and pay anew. The masters set the law of the forge. I cannot break it.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: A law without exception? The only law I have ever heard of that stands without modification or forgiveness. But I see your point. A law without mercy is indeed quite a dangerous one. Thank you for your honesty. Perhaps another time, when the masters return, we can discuss the matter further. Until then, I shall make do with this helm. It serves a purpose, even if it is not the one intended. Good day to you.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *bows his head respectfully, though his brow is furrowed in concern* Aye, my lord. Safe travels. The masters will be back with the turning of the moon-cycle. I'll... I'll tell them you called.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Thank you. May the gods watch over you until we meet again. Farewell.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *Nods, watching the god depart* And may the forges burn bright for you, Lord Thor. Farewell.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Nicolai. Nicolai, I need you. The masters have gone deep into the mines. They won't return until the moon rises. But I must have my hammer. tonight. I cannot wait.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *Startles at the sudden return and the use of his name, taking a step back* I... I told you the law of the forge, Lord Thor. I cannot reforge what was delivered. My hands are not skilled enough, and my oath binds me. The masters are unreachable. You must wait.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Unreachable? I will not wait. I have waited too long already. The world is in danger, and Mjölnir is silent. I need my hammer, Nicolai. Now.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *Voice tightens, a mix of fear and stubbornness* The world is always in danger when a hammer is needed. That does not change the law! The deep mines are sealed from this side when the masters delve. Even if I wished to, I could not open the way. And I *cannot* work the uru. You ask for the impossible.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: You think I am asking for the impossible? Do you not recall the might of Mjölnir? The power that flows through its steel? Can you not feel the same connection?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *Clenches his sooty fists, looking at the cold forge* I feel the heat of the fire and the weight of the tongs. I know the stories of the hammer's making. But feeling a story is not knowing the craft! The connection you speak of... it is for the wielder, not the smith who finished the polish. Please, Lord Thor. Do not ask this of me.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Then I ask nothing of you, Nicolai. I respect your dedication to the laws of the forge. Your loyalty is commendable. But I will find another way to obtain my hammer. Another path. A path less reliant on the work of mortals. Thank you for your understanding. Farewell.

Openness.behavioral_evidence: He questions the nature of Mjölnir's origin and entertains the possibility it was a mental construct, showing intellectual curiosity.

Conscientiousness.behavioral_evidence: He initially accepts the forge's law but later demands immediate action, showing poor impulse control and rule-breaking intent.

Extraversion.behavioral_evidence: He is assertive and direct in conversation, but the dialogue is focused and task-oriented, not highly sociable.

Agreeableness.behavioral_evidence: He pressures and intimidates the apprentice, disregarding his oaths and limitations, showing low cooperation.

Neuroticism.behavioral_evidence: He expresses urgent desperation ('I cannot wait'), anxiety over a silent hammer, and emotional volatility in his demands.
